edits.old: Embedded objects express exclusive ownership: one parent owns the embedded object, and removing that parent's reference or deleting the parent deletes it. edits.new: Embedded objects express exclusive ownership: a single parent owns the embedded object, and it is automatically deleted when the parent is deleted or when the parent no longer points at it. The .NET changelog records that linking to an already-managed embedded object historically threw an exception, though setting a property to the same embedded object it already holds is now a no-op.
